intro.heading: Atmospheric chemistry, air quality and climate
intro.description: Research spanning atmospheric aerosols, surface ozone, volatile organic compounds, indoor and outdoor air quality, transboundary haze and persistent organic pollutants, with a strong emphasis on measurements, source apportionment and policy-relevant evidence in Southeast Asia.

themes.title: Atmospheric Aerosols & Surfactants
themes.summary: Composition, sources and behaviour of atmospheric aerosols, including inorganic and organic constituents, surfactants, HULIS and the sea-surface microlayer.
themes.description: This research examines the chemical composition and sources of atmospheric particulate matter, with particular attention to surface-active substances, humic-like substances and the exchange of material between the sea-surface microlayer and the atmosphere. The work connects molecular-level characterisation to regional air quality, climate and human exposure.

themes.title: Surface Ozone, VOCs & Atmospheric Gases
themes.summary: Surface ozone, volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds, methane and the atmospheric chemistry that links emissions to air quality.
themes.description: Research on surface ozone and its precursors, including volatile organic compounds, semi-volatile organic compounds and methane. The work combines ambient measurements, source apportionment and modelling to understand ozone formation, nocturnal chemistry and the influence of land-use and climate change.

themes.title: Indoor & Outdoor Air Quality
themes.summary: Air quality in schools, homes, vehicles and urban environments, with a focus on exposure, health risk and practical monitoring.
themes.description: Indoor and outdoor air-quality research covering schools, residential buildings, vehicles, hospitals and urban spaces. The work examines particulate matter, trace gases, bioaerosols, dust and ventilation, and connects measured concentrations to human exposure and health risk.

themes.title: Regional Air Pollution, Haze & Climate
themes.summary: Transboundary haze, biomass burning, atmospheric transport, regional forecasting and the climate dimensions of air pollution.
themes.description: Regional-scale research on biomass burning, peatland fires, transboundary haze and the transport of air pollutants across Southeast Asia. The work includes forecasting systems, chemical weather modelling, long-term air-quality trends and the links between climate variability and pollution episodes.

themes.title: Persistent Organic Pollutants & Emerging Contaminants
themes.summary: Dioxins, furans, PCNs, PAHs, microplastics and other emerging contaminants in air, dust and coastal environments.
themes.description: Research on persistent organic pollutants and emerging contaminants, including polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans, polychlorinated naphthalenes, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and atmospheric microplastics. The work addresses sources, environmental distribution and human-health implications.

themes.title: Environmental Analytical Chemistry & Modelling
themes.summary: Sampling methods, analytical techniques, sensor systems and numerical models that underpin air-quality and atmospheric research.
themes.description: Method development and modelling research covering air sampling, chemical analysis, low-cost sensors, land-use regression, dispersion modelling and chemical weather prediction. This cross-cutting work supports the measurement and interpretation of air pollutants at local, national and regional scales.

impact.title: Policy-relevant air-quality evidence
impact.description: Research findings support Malaysian agencies including the Department of Environment and the Malaysian Meteorological Department, with work on air-quality indices, haze episodes, emissions and forecasting.

impact.title: International climate assessment
impact.description: Contribution to the IPCC Task Force Bureau on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories (TFI), connecting Malaysian atmospheric research to international climate assessment.

impact.title: Regional scientific leadership
impact.description: Leadership of MAAQR and involvement in IGAC-MANGO and SOLAS, supporting regional collaboration on atmospheric chemistry, air quality and climate.

impact.title: Research capacity building
impact.description: Supervision of 42 postgraduate researchers (43 supervision entries in the CV), including 27 completed PhDs, across atmospheric chemistry, air quality, climate and environmental health.

impact.title: Methods and monitoring
impact.description: Development and application of sampling methods, sensor systems, source-apportionment approaches and numerical models for air-quality assessment in Malaysia and Southeast Asia.
